description: Semantic dictionary and trigger signals for mapping raw notes and executive discussion points to deterministic 1-Pager layout primitives (Lego blocks).

kpi_row.name: KPI Metric Cards
kpi_row.semantic_intent: Highlighting 3~4 high-impact standalone quantitative metrics, performance baselines, or SLA deltas.
contextual_patterns: Statements containing numbers with units (%, ms, s, K, M, B, $, 萬, 億).
Comparative metrics with positive/negative trend symbols (▲, ▼, +, -).
Executive targets explicitly declared as annual or quarterly goals.
kpi_row.recommended_when: The note includes 3 to 4 distinct quantitative benchmarks that summarize executive outcomes.

card_grid.name: Strategic Theme Grid
card_grid.semantic_intent: Displaying 3~4 horizontal or symmetrical strategic pillars, thematic principles, or decoupled functional modules.
contextual_patterns: Items enumerated into 3 or 4 balanced, equal-weighted topics.
Categorization of an initiative into distinct operational departments or domains.
Parallel initiatives that execute concurrently without linear sequence.
card_grid.recommended_when: The discussion covers 3 to 4 parallel, non-chronological domains or strategic directives.

action_board.name: As-Is vs. To-Be Contrast Board
action_board.semantic_intent: Juxtaposing current operational deficits or pain points (As-Is / Red) directly against remedial solutions or future targets (To-Be / Green).
contextual_patterns: Direct pairing of problem statements with counteracting solutions.
Discussions evaluating migration from a legacy system to a newly proposed setup.
Contrasting manual bottlenecks with automated remediations.
action_board.recommended_when: The primary objective is problem diagnosis and countermeasure approval.

split_row.name: Dual-Track Symmetrical Split
split_row.semantic_intent: Framing two complementary topics, dual-track scopes, or head-to-head boundary definitions across left and right panels.
contextual_patterns: Explicit division into two balanced halves or operational tiers.
Scope boundary negotiations establishing what will and will not be delivered.
Dual-engine or dual-channel comparative specifications.
split_row.recommended_when: Content divides cleanly into two symmetrical categories or boundary contrasts.

anchor_card.name: Executive Anchor Policy Card
anchor_card.semantic_intent: Full-width anchor container emphasizing an overarching policy, binding compliance mandate, executive conclusion, or mathematical algorithm.
contextual_patterns: A single authoritative policy paragraph that sets the premise for all other blocks.
A core mathematical formula or operational equation.
A non-negotiable regulatory or security constraint.
anchor_card.recommended_when: The note requires a bold, foundational premise or authoritative policy statement across the canvas.

pipeline_flow.name: 4-Phase Horizontal SOP Pipeline
pipeline_flow.semantic_intent: Presenting a linear, sequential, 3 to 4 stage standard operating procedure (SOP) or lifecycle without branching.
contextual_patterns: Sequential numbering indicating chronological handoffs (Phase 01 -> Phase 02...).
Incident response playbooks with sequential containment steps.
Standard deployment, staging, and rollout lifecycles.
pipeline_flow.recommended_when: The note outlines a strict chronological progression across 3 to 4 discrete steps.

checklist_grid.name: Auditable Verification Checklist
checklist_grid.semantic_intent: Multi-item compliance verification, acceptance criteria, security audit requirements, or milestone tracking with check cues.
contextual_patterns: Actionable items with binary completion criteria (passed, pending, verified).
Numbered audit checkpoints before product or release sign-off.
Governance compliance clauses requiring explicit operator confirmation.
checklist_grid.recommended_when: Content specifies 4 to 6 discrete actionable verification items or audit controls.

flowchart.name: Service Topology Architecture (Mermaid)
flowchart.semantic_intent: Rendering distributed infrastructure, network ingress, routing paths, decoupled microservices, and persistent databases.
contextual_patterns: Descriptions of system entities passing data across tiers (clients -> gateway -> workers -> db).
Multi-branch architectural diagrams involving upstream and downstream dependencies.
High-availability clustering and active-passive failover mechanisms.
flowchart.recommended_when: The note details system architecture, component networking, or non-linear routing flows.

mermaid_sequence.name: API Handshake & Protocol Sequence
mermaid_sequence.semantic_intent: Visualizing chronological messaging between distinct actors, authentication handshakes, token verification, and RPC/HTTP calls.
contextual_patterns: Chronological dialogue: Actor A sends request -> Actor B validates -> Actor B queries Actor C.
Security token issuance, session refresh, and credential exchange workflows.
Error status code returns and retry handshake protocols.
mermaid_sequence.recommended_when: The primary focus is chronological inter-service communication or protocol validation.

mermaid_er.name: Database Schema & Entity Relationship
mermaid_er.semantic_intent: Documenting relational database structures, entity attributes, primary/foreign key mappings, and table cardinality.
contextual_patterns: Definitions of tables, schemas, and relational constraints between entities.
Data persistence models specifying fields, data types, and foreign key references.
Audit log schemas showing relationships between user actions and asset tables.
mermaid_er.recommended_when: The discussion centers on database modeling, data dictionary specs, or entity dependencies.

bar_chart.name: Discrete Benchmark Bar Chart
bar_chart.semantic_intent: Comparing categorical benchmark statistics, team output volumes, performance percentiles, or variance across units.
contextual_patterns: Discrete items compared along a single numeric axis (e.g., Team A: 45 vs. Team B: 80).
Quarterly or monthly metric shifts across predefined categories.
Performance benchmarks comparing throughput across different hardware or software configurations.
bar_chart.recommended_when: There are discrete, named categories requiring side-by-side quantitative visual comparison.

pie_chart.name: Proportional Share & Budget Breakdown
pie_chart.semantic_intent: Visualizing ratio composition, market share proportions, resource quotas, or budget splits that sum up to 100%.
contextual_patterns: Data components where percentages naturally add up to 100%.
Annual budget allocation split across engineering, operations, and security.
Asset distribution by cloud provider or environment tier.
pie_chart.recommended_when: The core message relates to proportional allocation or component shares of a whole.

matrix.name: Quadrant Priority Decision Matrix (2x2)
matrix.semantic_intent: Classifying tasks or investments into 4 distinct priority quadrants based on dual evaluation axes (e.g., Impact vs. Effort, Urgency vs. Importance).
contextual_patterns: Items categorized across two orthagonal scales (High/Low Impact vs. High/Low Cost).
Strategic backlog grooming allocating resources to Quick Wins vs. Long-term Bets.
Risk matrix categorizing likelihood versus consequence severity.
matrix.recommended_when: The document requires strategic prioritization or trade-off evaluation across 4 discrete quadrants.

zebra_table.name: Dense Multi-Column Zebra Table
zebra_table.semantic_intent: Organizing high-density, multi-column structured logs, compliance comparison matrices, asset registries, or feature specifications.
contextual_patterns: Data naturally organized into 3 or more distinct attribute headers (e.g., Domain | Standard | Status | Target Due Date).
Side-by-side feature compatibility matrices across vendors or solutions.
Formal compliance status records tracking requirements against verification dates.
zebra_table.recommended_when: Information contains structured rows and columns requiring clean vertical alignment and high reading density.
